policy_areas.name: route/auth/source-send approval
policy_areas.implementation: Shared route policy models the subscription -> direct_api -> openrouter ladder for all providers through Adapter capability facts and records route_step, route_steps, auth, billing, fallback, and source-send approval fields.
policy_areas.sync_guard: npm run lint:sync runs sync-provider-route-policy.mjs --check and sync-auth-selection.mjs --check

policy_areas.name: packet budgets
policy_areas.implementation: Shared source packet policy records source_packet_budget_bytes, selected_source_bytes, source_packet_within_budget, source_packet_action, resend_confirmation_required, review_surface_changed, and source_content_transmission. It blocks over-budget source-bearing packets before source send, blocks automatic resend after source-sent failures unless explicitly confirmed or narrowed, uses shared git diff packets for branch-diff review across subscription and direct API paths, and permits same-session no-source repair for substantive invalid-verdict prose without losing the original source attempt across failed no-source repair chains.

policy_areas.name: fallback semantics
policy_areas.interface: shared route ladder fallback ledger: subscription -> direct_api -> openrouter
policy_areas.implementation: Shared route ladder records attempted, selected, skipped_reason, and fallback_reason for subscription, direct_api, and openrouter. Adapter-specific transport choices, such as Grok CLI/web auto, are documented capability facts inside the selected shared route rather than alternate provider policy.

policy_areas.name: suggested actions

policy_areas.name: audit fields

policy_areas.name: review-quality gates

semantic_drift_policy.standard: Provider parity does not require fake parity or fake sameness. Every provider difference must have a clear reason: either an Adapter capability fact consumed by shared policy fields, a documented policy exception with evidence and tests, or an explicitly tracked noncompliance/research gap. Unclassified provider-specific semantics are drift.

exceptions.current_behavior: Grok has CLI/web subscription transports and local web fallback mechanics. The user-facing --transport auto flag is Grok-only because no other current provider Adapter has two subscription-backed transports to arbitrate between.
exceptions.capability_fact: Grok is the only current Adapter with two subscription-backed transports: CLI and local web tunnel.
exceptions.shared_policy_boundary: Shared policy records route_step=subscription, route_steps, selected_route, fallback_reason, auth_path, source_content_transmission, and runtime diagnostics; Grok transport auto only chooses between subscription transports and never changes the shared provider route ladder.
exceptions.clear_reason: This is an Adapter capability fact, not a provider-policy exception: shared route policy still treats Grok CLI and local web as subscription-route candidates, records route/fallback/source metadata, and forbids silent paid xAI API fallback. Providers with one subscription transport do not need a fake --transport auto flag; DeepSeek/GLM without subscription still enter the same subscription -> direct API -> OpenRouter ladder through capability facts.

exceptions.current_behavior: Kimi declares subscription capability only, rejects --auth-mode, and reports Kimi/Moonshot API env names as ignored. The shared route ledger still records subscription, direct_api, and openrouter steps with unsupported lower-route capability facts.
exceptions.capability_fact: The current Kimi Adapter implements a subscription-backed CLI transport and does not implement direct API or OpenRouter routes.
exceptions.shared_policy_boundary: Kimi flows through shared route_step and route_steps fields; unsupported direct API/OpenRouter states are Adapter capability facts, not separate Kimi policy.
exceptions.clear_reason: This is not fake parity: Kimi should not expose direct API or OpenRouter routes until an Adapter exists, but the shared route ladder already models those steps and will consume capability facts when they are added.

exceptions.current_behavior: DeepSeek uses the API reviewer path with direct API capability only. Shared route_steps records subscription_not_supported, direct_api selected, and openrouter unsupported/not_needed state.
exceptions.capability_fact: The current DeepSeek Adapter implements direct API auth and does not implement subscription CLI or OpenRouter routes.
exceptions.shared_policy_boundary: DeepSeek selects direct_api today through the same shared subscription -> direct_api -> openrouter route_steps ledger that explains subscription_not_supported and OpenRouter skip/fallback state.
exceptions.clear_reason: This is not fake parity: DeepSeek should not pretend to have a subscription CLI, but it must still enter the same shared route ladder and fall through by capability facts.

exceptions.current_behavior: GLM uses the API reviewer path with direct API capability only. Shared route_steps records subscription_not_supported, direct_api selected, and openrouter unsupported/not_needed state.
exceptions.capability_fact: The current GLM Adapter implements direct API auth and does not implement subscription CLI or OpenRouter routes.
exceptions.shared_policy_boundary: GLM selects direct_api today through the same shared subscription -> direct_api -> openrouter route_steps ledger that explains subscription_not_supported and OpenRouter skip/fallback state.
exceptions.clear_reason: This is not fake parity: GLM should not pretend to have a subscription CLI, but it must still enter the same shared route ladder and fall through by capability facts.

exceptions.current_behavior: Kimi has historical step_limit_exceeded and missing-verdict failures after source-bearing custom-review. Shared source packet policy now gates over-budget and automatic resend before source send, allows same-session no-source repair for substantive invalid-verdict prose, and carries the original source attempt through failed no-source repair chains. Any remaining within-budget Kimi step exhaustion is capacity evidence, not a Kimi-only policy path.
exceptions.shared_policy_boundary: Kimi step capacity must be represented as Adapter capacity facts consumed by evaluateSourcePacketPolicy, not as Kimi-only retry or source-send policy. Invalid-verdict repair is a shared retry-policy state for every session-capable companion, not a Kimi-only exception.
exceptions.clear_reason: This remains tracked because capacity limits may require future capability facts, but the source-send decision, resend gate, and no-source repair policy are now shared with every provider.

guardrail_tests.name: provider parity table contract
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when the canonical provider parity table is missing required providers, policy areas, issue fit, evidence, or schema shape.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: provider-parity-table.json is missing or omits a required FR-002 policy area.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: provider-parity-table.json parses and satisfies the checked schema/policy inventory.

guardrail_tests.name: provider semantic drift classification
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when a provider-specific difference is not classified as an Adapter capability fact, documented policy exception, known accidental drift, or research gap with a clear reason and shared-policy boundary.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: A provider exception lacks difference_type, capability_fact, shared_policy_boundary, clear_reason, evidence, tests, or verdict; an intentional difference is not an allowed capability/policy exception.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: Every provider difference is explicitly classified, evidence-backed, test-backed, and tied to the shared policy boundary so fake parity is not required and unclassified drift is blocked.

guardrail_tests.name: full provider policy surface
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when the shared Provider Policy Interface stops covering one of the required cross-provider policy domains.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: buildProviderPolicyContract omits a provider, route step, or policy domain, or the parity table's guardrail inventory no longer matches the generated contract.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: The generated Provider Policy Interface and parity table both enumerate the same provider-neutral policy domains for all six providers.

guardrail_tests.name: shared audit/status field inventory
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when generated provider-neutral contracts stop naming shared audit/status fields.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: renderExternalModelContractDoc omits a shared audit/status field.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: Generated contract docs contain the complete shared field inventory.

guardrail_tests.name: shared policy interface usage
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when provider-facing entrypoints or synced libs stop consuming required shared policy interfaces.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: A required shared interface is absent from provider-facing source or the parity table.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: The interface inventory is explicit and each required interface is present in provider-facing source.

guardrail_tests.name: source packet pre-send enforcement
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when a source-bearing launch path records source packet policy without enforcing it before provider launch.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: A provider runtime can build a review audit manifest but does not inspect source_packet_policy.source_send_allowed before launching the provider transport.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: Claude, Gemini, Kimi, Grok, DeepSeek, and GLM launch paths all stop over-budget source packets before source send through the shared source packet policy.

guardrail_tests.name: grok auto transport fallback
guardrail_tests.purpose: Fail when Grok auto transport stops preserving CLI default, audited local web fallback, or no-paid-API guarantees.
guardrail_tests.red_condition: GROK_TRANSPORT=auto is rejected, falls back to paid API credentials, fails to record CLI-to-web fallback metadata, or reintroduces a Grok-local source-transmission policy helper.
guardrail_tests.green_condition: Auto mode records CLI success as CLI, approved CLI failure fallback as local web with source disclosure, prompt-budget failures preserve CLI diagnostics, and Grok uses shared sourceContentTransmissionForExecution.
